Why a private guide

Why a private tour guide in Rio

Rio is big, hilly and spread out. The Christ the Redeemer statue, Sugarloaf and the beaches are far from each other, and traffic and clouds change the plan every day.

A private guide handles that for you. You get picked up at your hotel, you skip the guesswork about when to go where, and you can ask questions without raising your hand in a group of thirty. If the summit is covered in cloud, we swap the order and go back later.

I speak English every day with visitors, so you'll understand the stories behind the places and not just the names.

If you're traveling alone and only want the highlights, a group tour may be enough. For families, couples who don't want to rush, or anyone who needs fluent English, a private tour usually pays off.

In Portuguese

How to say it in Portuguese

If you're searching in Portuguese, the term is guia de turismo (the licensed professional) or guia turístico. A tour guide who speaks English is a guia que fala inglês. Brazilian law regulates the profession of Guia de Turismo (Law 8.623/1993) [CONFIRM CURRENT TEXT].
